note: Found on 2026-10-02. A Wenner sheet of resistances whose apparent resistivity holds at 9 ohm-m to a = 12 m and halves by 15 m, a drop no layered earth makes. The second layer's resistivity runs to the 0.5 ohm-m bound and no inversion converges: Python reports, unconverged, a fit of 15.26 percent after its 60 iterations, 15.14 after 200 and a three-layer 13.14 after 2000. The browser stopped at its own 60 iterations at 15.19 percent with a different boundary (11.14 m against 11.20 m). That was put down to the iteration cap, but both engines run the same search with the same cap; what differed was the Wenner potential, an integral over J0, which the browser evaluated with quadrature tables built from Numerical Recipes' J0 and J1, good to 5e-9. With the tables built from Cephes j0 and j1, as scipy's are, both engines stop at 15.2557 percent with the boundary at 11.2032 m. Perturbing Python's forward model by 1e-15 to 1e-10 as a cosine in the log of the spacing moves its answer by at most 7.2e-11; over the four shapes, and readings perturbed as well, at up to 1e-7 every closed VES case moves by at most 1.6e-4. The question the case was held open for stands for the owner as a product question: what should be reported for an inversion that has not converged when max_iterations runs out? Today both engines report the model where it stopped, with converged = False and nothing in the report saying so.
